title: Odisha evacuates 1.2 lakh, 69 trains cancelled as Cyclone Akvan approaches with 110 kmph gusts; AP on red alert - The New Indian Express

full_text:
Odisha has evacuated more than 1.20 lakh people from vulnerable areas and deployed over 300 rescue teams as it stepped up preparations ahead of severe cyclonic storm Akvan, which is expected to cross the North Andhra Pradesh and South Odisha coasts close to Gopalpur by noon on Friday, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said.
In its latest update issued on Thursday evening, the IMD said Akvan was moving northwards at 13 kmph and lay over the west-central Bay of Bengal at 5.30 pm, centred near latitude 16.1°N and longitude 85.2°E. It was about 350 km south of Gopalpur, 420 km south of Puri, 380 km east of Narsapur in Andhra Pradesh and 270 km south-southeast of Kalingapatnam.
The system is likely to move north-northwestwards before crossing the coast near Gopalpur by noon on November 20, with maximum sustained wind speeds of 90-100 kmph and gusts reaching 110 kmph, the IMD said.
The Odisha government has set up 9,299 cyclone shelters across potentially affected districts. The storm's projected path has shifted towards Odisha over the past 24 hours after initially being forecast to make landfall along the Andhra Pradesh coast.
Chief Secretary Anu Garg said 45,364 people had been evacuated in Ganjam and 18,000 in Gajapati. The government has deployed 60 teams of the Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force (ODRAF), 14 teams of the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and 131 teams of the Fire and Emergency Services. It has also asked the Indian Coast Guard to keep its helicopters, vessels and other logistics ready for rescue and relief operations.
Arrangements are being made at cyclone shelters to provide cooked and dry food, essential medicines, drinking water, sanitary napkins and other facilities, Garg said.
Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari said the government had identified 941 landslide-prone locations across Ganjam, Gajapati, Kandhamal, Koraput and Malkangiri districts. Gajapati accounted for the highest number, with 211 such locations.
He said 10 people had died in landslides during the previous cyclone, Arnab. Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi, who reviewed the state's preparedness, stressed the need to maintain the government's zero-casualty mission.
The approaching storm has also disrupted rail services. The East Coast Railway cancelled 41 trains and rescheduled 29 others, while the South Eastern Railway cancelled at least 28 express trains, mostly those bound for or passing through Puri on Friday.
Among the cancelled services are the Bhubaneswar-Visakhapatnam, Howrah-Puri and Tatanagar-Brahmapur Vande Bharat Express trains, as well as the Puri-Yesvantpur Garib Rath Express. The Howrah-Puri-Howrah Vande Bharat Express has also been cancelled for Friday.
Tourists have been prohibited from visiting coastal areas, including Gopalpur, Puri, Satapada and Chilika, while fishermen have been advised not to venture into the sea. The coastal and southern parts of Odisha have been receiving light to moderate rain since Wednesday night, with rainfall expected to intensify as the system approaches, Bhubaneswar Meteorological Centre Director Manorama Mohanty said.
Educational institutions in districts under red, orange and yellow warnings have been closed, an official said. Rescue teams have been deployed in Malkangiri, Koraput, Rayagada, Kalahandi, Gajapati, Ganjam, Kandhamal, Boudh, Puri, Nayagarh and Khurda districts.
The Gundicha Temple in Puri will remain closed to visitors from November 19 to 21. The 12th-century Jagannath Temple, however, will remain open, with daily rituals continuing as usual. Shree Jagannath Temple Administration Chief Administrator Arabinda Padhee urged devotees to plan their visits in accordance with weather advisories.
The Nandankanan Zoological Park and the adjoining State Botanical Garden in Bhubaneswar will remain closed on November 19 and 20. The Bhitarkanika National Park has been closed until November 21, while the Similipal Tiger Reserve will remain closed to visitors on November 20 and 21.
In Andhra Pradesh, the IMD has issued a red alert for Srikakulam and Vizianagaram districts, warning of extremely heavy rainfall at isolated places. An orange alert has been issued for Parvatipuram Manyam, Alluri Sitaramaraju and Anakapalli districts, while Kakinada is under a yellow alert.
The Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority has advised people in North Andhra to remain alert, urged farmers to take precautions during agricultural activities and asked fishermen not to venture into the sea.
Under the IMD's rainfall warning categories, a red alert indicates extremely heavy rainfall exceeding 20.44 cm in 24 hours. An orange alert denotes very heavy rainfall of 11.56 cm to 20.44 cm, while a yellow alert indicates heavy rainfall of 6.45 cm to 11.55 cm.
(With inputs from PTI)

NEW DELHI: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast thunderstorms, lightning, gusty winds and rainfall across several states over the next few days. Cyclone Akvan is expected to cross the North Andhra Pradesh-Yanam and South Odisha coasts between Narsapur and Puri by noon on November 20, bringing strong winds and heavy rainfall to several parts of the eastern coast.
The storm is likely to make landfall with maximum sustained wind speeds of 90-100 kmph, gusting to 110 kmph. Several states, including Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Tamil Nadu and Jharkhand, are likely to experience the impact of the system.
Delhi-NCR weather tomorrow
The IMD has forecast dense fog at isolated places across Delhi, Haryana, Chandigarh and Punjab on November 20. East and West Uttar Pradesh are also likely to experience dense fog during this period.
The latest IMD bulletin has not specified a temperature forecast for Delhi.
Andhra Pradesh weather tomorrow
Cyclone Akvan is expected to cross the North Andhra Pradesh-Yanam coast between Narsapur and Puri, close to the east of Gopalpur, by noon on November 20.
The IMD has issued an orange cyclone alert for the Andhra Pradesh and adjoining south Odisha coasts. North coastal Andhra Pradesh may receive extremely heavy rainfall at isolated places on November 20, with rainfall likely to affect several other parts of the state.
Rough sea conditions and high-intensity waves have been reported along the Srikakulam coast. Fishermen have suspended fishing activities, with boats and motorised vessels anchored along the coastline.
Odisha weather tomorrow
Odisha is likely to receive light to moderate rainfall at most places, with heavy to very heavy rainfall at isolated locations on November 20 and 21.
The Rayagada district administration has identified around 55 landslide-prone villages for possible evacuation. The district has been issued yellow and orange weather warnings for November 20.
The state government has evacuated nearly 72,000 people from vulnerable districts and identified 7,900 shelters. Around 60 Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force (ODRAF) teams, 14 National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) teams and 131 Fire Services teams have been deployed.
Schools, colleges and Anganwadi centres in six vulnerable districts have also been ordered to remain closed from November 20 to 21.
Telangana weather tomorrow
Cyclone Akvan is likely to affect Telangana after crossing the Andhra Pradesh coast. Four eastern districts of the state have been placed under an orange alert for November 20.
Tamil Nadu weather tomorrow
North Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal are likely to receive light to moderate rainfall at many places on November 20, with heavy rainfall forecast at isolated locations.
The IMD had also forecast heavy to very heavy rainfall at isolated places on November 19, which could lead to waterlogging in parts of Tamil Nadu.
Jharkhand weather tomorrow
The impact of Cyclone Akvan is likely to bring rainfall to southern and central parts of Jharkhand from Thursday evening.
The IMD has issued a yellow alert for heavy rainfall in 11 districts on Friday. These include Lohardaga, Gumla, Simdega, Ramgarh, Ranchi, Khunti, Bokaro, Dhanbad, Saraikela-Kharsawan, West Singhbhum and East Singhbhum.
Thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds are also expected from Thursday evening. The weather department has forecast a decline in rainfall intensity from Sunday, with clear skies likely from November 23.
Northeast India weather tomorrow
Assam and Meghalaya are likely to receive isolated to scattered rainfall between November 20 and 22. Thunderstorms and lightning are also expected over the two states on November 19.
Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura may receive isolated to scattered rainfall on November 22. Thunderstorms and lightning are likely over these states on November 19 and 20.
IMD's latest forecast for the next few days
The IMD has forecast heavy rainfall in parts of Odisha and Jharkhand on November 20 and 21, with the impact of Cyclone Akvan likely to extend to neighbouring states.
In Jharkhand, eight districts are also expected to receive heavy rainfall on November 21 and 22. These include Giridih, Dhanbad, Deoghar, Jamtara, Dumka, Godda, Pakur and Sahibganj.
The weather department has also forecast a decline in rainfall intensity in Jharkhand from Sunday, with clear skies expected from November 23.

Cyclone Akvan: IMD Issues Red Alert For Andhra Districts, 28 Trains Cancelled Ahead Of Landfall
Cyclone Akvan is expected to cross the Andhra-Odisha coast on Friday with winds reaching 110 kmph. The IMD has issued weather alerts, while 28 express trains have been cancelled as a precaution.
- Cyclone Akvan to cross North Andhra-Odisha coasts by Friday.
- Red alerts issued for districts expecting extremely heavy rainfall.
- Over 28 trains cancelled due to approaching Cyclone Akvan.
Severe cyclonic storm Akvan is expected to cross the coasts of North Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and South Odisha near Gopalpur by noon on Friday, November 20, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has warned. The storm is likely to bring winds of 90-100 kmph, with gusts reaching 110 kmph. Authorities have issued weather alerts across several districts, while the South Eastern Railway has cancelled at least 28 trains as a precautionary measure ahead of the cyclone's landfall.
Red Alert Issued
According to the IMD, Akvan was located over the west-central Bay of Bengal at 2.30 pm on Thursday. It lay approximately 390 km east-south-east of Narsapur, 320 km south-south-east of Kalingapatnam and 410 km south of Gopalpur.
The weather department said the cyclone, which was initially expected to cross the coast along mid-coastal Andhra Pradesh, subsequently changed course towards North Andhra Pradesh and Odisha.
A red alert has been issued for Srikakulam and Vizianagaram districts, while Parvatipuram Manyam, Alluri Sitaramaraju and Anakapalli are under an orange alert. Kakinada has been placed under a yellow alert.
Extremely heavy rainfall is expected at isolated places in Srikakulam and Vizianagaram. Heavy to very heavy rainfall is forecast in the orange alert districts, while Kakinada may receive heavy rainfall.
The Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority has advised residents of North Andhra to remain alert. Farmers have been urged to take precautions, while fishermen have been warned against venturing into the sea.

28 Trains Cancelled
Meanwhile, the South Eastern Railway has cancelled at least 28 express trains scheduled for Thursday and Friday due to the approaching cyclone.
Several services connecting Puri and other parts of Odisha, West Bengal and Jharkhand have been affected.
The Shalimar-Puri Express and Bhanjpur-Puri Express, scheduled to depart on Thursday, have been cancelled. The Howrah-Puri-Howrah Vande Bharat Express will also remain cancelled on Friday.
Other affected services include the Puri-Bhanjpur Express, Bangriposi-Puri-Bangriposi Express and Brahmapur-Tatanagar-Brahmapur Express.
Several passenger trains operating across Odisha and neighbouring Jharkhand have also been cancelled as a precautionary measure.
What Do The Alerts Mean?
The IMD's rainfall alerts indicate the expected intensity of precipitation:
- Red alert: Extremely heavy rainfall exceeding 20.44 cm in 24 hours.
- Orange alert: Very heavy rainfall between 11.56 cm and 20.44 cm.
- Yellow alert: Heavy rainfall between 6.45 cm and 11.55 cm.
